characteristics.cultivar: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis (Chinese varietals introduced by the British)
characteristics.harvestSeason: March–April, immediately following spring bud burst
characteristics.teaware: Teapot or gaiwan, best without milk

description.short: The most prized and costly harvest of the year — pale, greenish, floral, and extraordinarily delicate, almost like an oolong
description.overview: Revered as the 'Champagne of Teas', Darjeeling's first flush is especially prized for its delicate floral profile, standing in stark contrast to typical bold Indian black teas.
description.leaf: Twisted, light greenish-brown leaf, less dense than the second flush
description.aroma: Floral and fresh with notes of muscatel green grapes
description.taste: Light, delicate, floral with minimal astringency — tea connoisseurs enjoy it pure without milk, much like a green or lightly oxidized oolong tea
description.processing: Plucking tender spring shoots right after winter dormancy → brief withering → gentle rolling → light oxidation (lighter than conventional black tea) → drying

history.origin: Darjeeling plantations were founded by the British in the 1840s in territory formerly belonging to Nepal, using Chinese (rather than Assamica) tea seeds and cultivars.
history.development: The unique terroir — high elevation, mist, and diurnal temperature swings — combined with small-leaf Chinese cultivars produced a cup profile unlike any other Indian tea.
history.modern: Darjeeling was India's first registered Geographical Indication (GI); the spring first flush is traditionally the most expensive and commands high bids at international auctions.
interestingFacts: Darjeeling is the only major tea region in India historically planted with Camellia sinensis var. sinensis bushes rather than assamica, giving it its distinct refined profile.
Due to the short harvesting window and worldwide acclaim, first flush Darjeeling lots are frequently presold to collectors and premier tea merchants before picking even concludes.
